name: King's Indian Defense
description: Let White take the centre, then strike back with …e5 and a kingside attack.

lines.name: 8.d5 Ne7

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …e5 is Black's central strike; it fixes the centre for the plans to come.
notes.13: …Nc6 adds pressure on d4 and invites d5.
notes.15: …Ne7 heads to the kingside, where Black plays …f5 next.

lines.summary: Fianchetto, castle, strike with …e5; when White locks the centre with d5, attack with …f5.

lines.name: Mar del Plata (9.Ne1)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …e5 is Black's central strike; it fixes the centre for the plans to come.
notes.13: …Nc6 adds pressure on d4 and invites d5.
notes.15: …Ne7 heads to the kingside, where Black plays …f5 next.
notes.19: …f5 opens the kingside fight; White attacks on the queenside.
notes.23: …f4 gains space; next come …g5-g4 and a direct attack on White's king.

lines.summary: The race: Black storms the kingside with …f5, …f4, …g5; White pushes c5 on the queenside.

lines.name: Bayonet (9.b4)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …e5 is Black's central strike; it fixes the centre for the plans to come.
notes.13: …Nc6 adds pressure on d4 and invites d5.
notes.15: …Ne7 heads to the kingside, where Black plays …f5 next.
notes.21: …Nf6 brings the knight back to the centre and covers h7 against the g5 knight.

lines.summary: Against b4, go for …Nh5 and …f5 straight away; speed matters in the race.

lines.name: Exchange (7.dxe5)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …e5 is Black's central strike; it fixes the centre for the plans to come.
notes.13: …dxe5 recaptures; the queens come off but Black is fine.
notes.15: …Rxd8 takes the open file; the d4 square is a good outpost for a black knight.

lines.summary: The early queen trade isn't scary: take with the rook and aim a knight at d4.

lines.name: Petrosian (7.d5)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …e5 is Black's central strike; it fixes the centre for the plans to come.
notes.13: …a5 slows White's b4 push on the queenside.
notes.15: …h6 asks the bishop to decide; it can't keep the pin forever.
notes.17: …Na6 heads for c5, a great square for the knight.
notes.19: …Qe8 unpins the f6 knight so Black can play …Nh7 and …f5.

lines.summary: Against an early d5, stop b4 with …a5, then knight to c5 and break the pin before …f5.

lines.name: Samisch (5.f3)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.9: …O-O first; White's f3 means a kingside pawn storm may come.
notes.11: …e5 hits the centre, the same answer as against the Classical.
notes.13: …Nh5 prepares …f5 and eyes the f4 square.
notes.15: …f5 strikes at e4, Black's main lever in the King's Indian.

lines.summary: Against f3 and Be3, play …e5, then …Nh5 and …f5 to break up White's pawn centre.

lines.name: Four Pawns Attack (5.f4)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.
notes.11: …c5 attacks the overextended centre right away.
notes.13: …e6 breaks open the e-file against White's uncastled king.
notes.17: …Bg4 pins the f3 knight, which supports White's e5 push.

lines.summary: The big pawn centre is a target: hit it with …c5 and …e6, then pin the f3 knight.

lines.name: Fianchetto (g3)

notes.3: …g6 prepares …Bg7, a bishop that will press on the long diagonal.

lines.summary: Against the fianchetto, play …Nbd7, …e5 and …c6: a solid centre with ideas of …Qb6.

lines.name: vs the London (2.Bf4)

notes.3: …g6: the same King's Indian set-up works against the London.
notes.9: …d6 prepares …e5 or …c5 against White's quiet set-up.
notes.11: …c5 hits d4 and opens the long diagonal for the g7 bishop.

lines.summary: Against the London, keep the fianchetto and strike with …c5 at d4.
